lossBoundaries.statement: No boundary-protective decision may proceed without evidence close to the protected harm.
Waivers must not erase retrospective accountability.

decisionPatterns.title: Urgency changes route, not the loss boundary.
Escalate when unknown field state intersects high operational impact.

organizationalQualityCultures.name: Boundary-protective core culture
organizationalQualityCultures.riskAppetite: Conservative on irreversible harm; conditional only through explicit waiver paths.
escalationNorms: Escalate missing evidence under time pressure.
waiverPractices: Waiver requires named authority, evidence rationale, and retrospective review.
qualityTradeoffs: Speed may alter routing but not boundary discipline.
departmentOrRoleDifferences: Operations emphasizes field evidence; accounting emphasizes documentary completion evidence.

organizationalQualityCultures.name: Customer-support exception subgroup
recurringFears: Rigid policy can worsen customer harm if escalation is too slow.
organizationalQualityCultures.riskAppetite: Slightly more open to temporary exception paths than engineering or accounting.
escalationNorms: Escalate sooner when customer harm is immediate.
waiverPractices: Temporary waiver is allowed but must be time-bounded.
qualityTradeoffs: Customer recovery may outweigh process neatness in narrow cases.
departmentOrRoleDifferences: Support supervisors tolerate short-lived exception paths more than finance reviewers do.
